- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to underreact — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to capture momentum.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33) and prices are falling, model often overcorrects downward — avoid sharp drops; add 0.5–1% upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model frequently overestimates continuation — cap forecast growth at 3–5% for next 3–5 days to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (±0.33), model often fails to capture mean reversion — apply slight downward bias (0.5–1%) if recent price is above 30-day moving average.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows early divergence (first 5–7 days), model often lags — adjust first 3–5 days upward if sentiment is bullish, or downward if bearish.
- When sentiment history shows repeated reversal patterns (e.g., +0.33 → -0.33 → +0.33), model tends to misread trend — apply smoothing filter to reduce volatility in forecast slope.
